claims.text: The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr RHEA is a single-phase disordered BCC alloy.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has high density.
The baseline Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has insufficient room-temperature ductility.
A minor Al addition to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will induce precipitation of a discrete ordered B2 phase.
Controlled heat treatment of the Al-modified alloy will induce BCC/B2 phase decomposition.
The resulting microstructure will have a continuous disordered BCC matrix and a reticulated network of discrete ordered B2 precipitates.
The B2 precipitates will be enriched in Al.
The B2 precipitate network will mitigate crack propagation by causing crack deflection or bridging.
A continuous BCC matrix retains the ductility required for plastic deformation.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix produces poor room-temperature ductility.
An inverted BCC+B2 topology will improve room-temperature compressive ductility while maintaining high yield strength.
The Al-modified alloy will attain more than 10% room-temperature compressive ductility.
The inverted BCC+B2 alloy will maintain high yield strength.
The Al-modified alloy will have significantly greater yield strength than the baseline single-phase alloy.
Adding Al and forming B2 will cause a marginal density increase relative to the Al-free baseline.
The modified alloy will have lower density than traditional W/Ta-based RHEAs.
The useful Al concentration lies above the threshold for B2 precipitation but below the concentration that produces a continuous B2 matrix.
Excessive Al may cause brittle Laves phases to form in this alloy.
The baseline alloy is brittle because it lacks a ductile continuous matrix or effective crack-arresting mechanisms.
About 2-4 at% Al will produce discrete B2, whereas more than 8 at% Al will produce a continuous B2 phase.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts a marginal density increase and the predicted outcome initially states that density increases with Al content, but the uncertainty field acknowledges that low-density Al generally lowers density and that the modified density may instead be lower or comparable.

The baseline is described as single-phase BCC yet is also said to lack a ductile continuous matrix, while the proposed mechanism identifies a continuous BCC matrix as the ductile constituent. A single-phase BCC baseline is itself a continuous BCC matrix unless an additional distinction is supplied.
